records.Concise description: ACINQ's Scala/JVM implementation of the Lightning Network, designed for production-scale node operation.
records.Deeper researched summary: Eclair is an open-source Lightning implementation written in Scala and built around the JVM/actor model. ACINQ uses Eclair in its own Lightning infrastructure and maintains the code independently from LND and Core Lightning, giving the network additional implementation diversity. Its production architecture and feature set are implementation-specific; public descriptions of routing, trampoline, splicing, offers, or other capabilities should be rechecked against current releases.
Creators / founders: ACINQ engineering team and Eclair contributors
records.Launch / history: Eclair development began in 2015 and became part of ACINQ's Lightning production stack. The canonical repository had active commits through August 14, 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin network ec: It is one of the principal interoperable Lightning implementations and demonstrates a distinct JVM/Scala production architecture.
records.Verification basis: Official ACINQ repository and operator documentation establish Eclair's identity, production role, language, and active 2026 maintenance.
Research notes / uncertainties: Phoenix is a WALLETS entity and should not be duplicated here.
Do not freeze ACINQ's historical node size, channel count, or capacity into canonical copy.
Reverify rapidly evolving protocol-feature support before publication.

records.Concise description: A modular Lightning implementation packaged as an SDK for embedding Lightning functionality into applications across environments.
records.Deeper researched summary: LDK is not primarily a monolithic daemon: its core design exposes Lightning state machines, routing, chain interaction, persistence, key management, and networking as composable modules that an application can combine with its own infrastructure. The broader LDK ecosystem also includes higher-level node products, but MSC keeps one canonical LDK profile and treats LDK Node/LDK Server as related products rather than duplicate entities. Current 2026 documentation and engineering posts show active work on features such as async payments and modern offers/onion-message flows.
records.Launch / history: LDK grew from the rust-lightning implementation and developed into a multi-language Lightning SDK. Current documentation and blog activity continued through June 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin network ec: It makes Lightning available as embeddable infrastructure rather than forcing applications to run an external monolithic node daemon, broadening wallet, mobile, server, and custom-node design space.
Important technical or cultural characte: Custom chain source, storage, networking, and keys
Can build full nodes without being a daemon itself
records.Verification basis: Current official documentation and 2026 project publications establish active maintenance and clearly distinguish LDK's SDK architecture from a packaged daemon.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not conflate LDK core with LDK Node or LDK Server; keep them as child/related products.
Feature support is configuration- and version-dependent; reverify before public copy.

records.Concise description: Blockstream's hosted infrastructure for remotely operated Core Lightning nodes in which users retain signing keys while Blockstream runs node infrastructure.
records.Deeper researched summary: Greenlight provisions and operates Core Lightning node infrastructure while keeping key-control responsibilities separated from the hosted server. Current Blockstream documentation describes hosted, non-custodial Lightning nodes and exposes Core Lightning interfaces to applications. This is operationally distinct from self-hosting: the service provider runs infrastructure even though user-controlled keys are intended to preserve spending authority. That separation makes Greenlight canon-worthy as a distinct network infrastructure model rather than a duplicate Core Lightning profile.
records.Launch / history: Greenlight was introduced as Blockstream-managed Lightning infrastructure and remains documented as an active service in 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin network ec: It demonstrates a hosted-node architecture that separates infrastructure operation from key custody, a major design pattern for wallets and Lightning services that want node functionality without operating all server components.
records.Verification basis: Current Blockstream documentation was checked for hosted architecture, Core Lightning relationship, and key-control model.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not describe Greenlight as self-hosting; Blockstream operates infrastructure.
'Non-custodial' describes the intended key-control architecture, not absence of operational trust or service dependency.

records.Concise description: An open-source Bitcoin mempool and block explorer with fee estimation, transaction visualization, API services, mining views, Lightning views, and self-hosting support.
records.Deeper researched summary: mempool.space combines a public hosted service with open-source frontend/backend software that can be self-hosted. It visualizes unconfirmed transactions, block inclusion projections, fees, replacements, blocks, mining data, and additional Bitcoin/Lightning metrics. Its fee estimates, block projections, transaction labels, mining interpretations, and graph views are application-level analyses built from node/indexer data; they are not Bitcoin consensus state or guarantees of miner behavior.
Creators / founders: mempool.space / Mempool Open Source Project contributors
records.Launch / history: The project emerged in the late 2010s and has grown into a broad Bitcoin explorer/observability stack. Version 3.3.1 was released April 21, 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin network ec: It is one of the most visible ways users and operators inspect Bitcoin's mempool and blocks and is also widely self-hosted alongside personal nodes.
records.Verification basis: Current hosted service and official repository/release evidence establish active operation and open-source/self-hosting scope.
Research notes / uncertainties: Fee estimates and block projections are estimates, not consensus rules or guarantees of miner inclusion.
Labels, classifications, mining attribution, and Lightning statistics are indexer/application interpretations.
Do not freeze time-sensitive mempool or network metrics into timeless profile copy.
